legend: Emuskald is an avid horticulturist and owns the world's longest greenhouse — it is effectively infinite in length.

Over the years Emuskald has cultivated n plants in his greenhouse, of m different plant species numbered from 1 to m. His greenhouse is very narrow and can be viewed as an infinite line, with each plant occupying a single point on that line.

Emuskald has discovered that each species thrives at a different temperature, so he wants to arrange m - 1 borders that would divide the greenhouse into m sections numbered from 1 to m from left to right with each section housing a single species. He is free to place the borders, but in the end all of the i-th species plants must reside in i-th section from the left.

Of course, it is not always possible to place the borders in such way, so Emuskald needs to replant some of his plants. He can remove each plant from its position and place it anywhere in the greenhouse (at any real coordinate) with no plant already in it. Since replanting is a lot of stress for the plants, help Emuskald find the minimum number of plants he has to replant to be able to place the borders.
input: The first line of input contains two space-separated integers n and m (1 ≤ n, m ≤ 5000, n ≥ m), the number of plants and the number of different species. Each of the following n lines contain two space-separated numbers: one integer number si (1 ≤ si ≤ m), and one real number xi (0 ≤ xi ≤ 109), the species and position of the i-th plant. Each xi will contain no more than 6 digits after the decimal point.

It is guaranteed that all xi are different; there is at least one plant of each species; the plants are given in order "from left to the right", that is in the ascending order of their xi coordinates (xi < xi + 1, 1 ≤ i < n).
output: Output a single integer — the minimum number of plants to be replanted.
note: In the first test case, Emuskald can replant the first plant to the right of the last plant, so the answer is 1.
In the second test case, the species are already in the correct order, so no replanting is needed.

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含两个以空格分隔的整数 n 和 m（1 ≤ n, m ≤ 5000，n ≥ m），分别表示植物的数量和不同物种的数量。接下来的 n 行中，每行包含两个以空格分隔的数：一个整数 si（1 ≤ si ≤ m），表示物种；以及一个实数 xi（0 ≤ xi ≤ 109），表示第 i 株植物的位置。每个 xi 的小数点后不超过 6 位。
保证所有 xi 互不相同；每个物种至少有一株植物；植物按照“从左到右”的顺序给出，即其 xi 坐标按升序排列（xi < xi + 1，1 ≤ i < n）。

output.ai: 输出一个整数——需要重新种植的植物数量的最小值。

note.ai: 在第一个测试用例中，Emuskald 可以将第一株植物重新种植到最后一株植物的右侧，因此答案为 1。
在第二个测试用例中，各植物的物种已经处于正确顺序，因此不需要重新种植。

legend.ai: Emuskald 是一位狂热的园艺爱好者，拥有世界上最长的温室——它的长度实际上是无限的。
多年来，Emuskald 在他的温室中培育了 n 株植物，它们属于 m 个不同的植物物种，编号为 1 到 m。他的温室非常狭窄，可以看作一条无限长的直线，每株植物占据直线上的一个点。
Emuskald 发现每个物种在不同的温度下生长得最好，因此他想设置 m - 1 个分界线，将温室划分为 m 个区域，从左到右编号为 1 到 m，并让每个区域只种植一个物种。他可以自由放置这些分界线，但最终所有第 i 个物种的植物都必须位于从左数第 i 个区域内。
当然，并不总能以这种方式放置分界线，因此 Emuskald 需要重新种植一部分植物。他可以将每株植物从原来的位置移走，并将其放置在温室中的任意位置（任意实数坐标处），但该位置不能已有其他植物。由于重新种植会给植物带来很大的压力，请帮助 Emuskald 找出为了能够放置这些分界线，他至少需要重新种植多少株植物。
